pr_body:
Fixes #4683

This creates a `@parcel/resolver-glob` plugin which resolves glob specifiers. It's not currently in the default config, but can be enabled by adding it to your `.parcelrc`. It works identically to the Parcel v1 version for JS, and also works for CSS. In addition, it works with pipelines like `url:`, and also for dynamic import. See the tests for examples.

Is this PR expected to be merged soon? For now, I am going to just load the url for each file in my directory individually.

(Is there some other plugin I should use instead for now?)

Thanks!
I also need this. Would be great if it will be merged. Thanks!

Very much anticipating this functionality. Doing "animated PNGs" in my current project, which currently involves importing each frame image separately... Loving Parcel, but being able to eliminate hundreds of lines of repetitive code would be a great boon.
This PR would also benefit a lot a project I'm working on with parcel.

We encountered the node-gyp/deasync problem in Parcel 1 (#5294), so we tried to upgrade to Parcel 2. It doesn't do glob imports, so we can't use it. This PR fixes that problem, but 3 months have passed with no activity. So we're stuck on old versions of Node and Parcel. I'd rather not have to move everything off Parcel and onto esbuild, but if this isn't fixed then I'll have to eventually.

Can you use the babel plugin in the meantime? https://github.com/devongovett/babel-plugin-transform-glob-import

I believe the current state was that there was disagreement among the core team about how dynamic import should be handled. I hope to get back to this soon.
@devongovett Thanks, I'll give it a try.
@RickyRomero When you're done, could you let us know how it goes for you? Thanks!

@devongovett @DarthFloopy Here's where I got following [the migration guide for Parcel 2](https://v2.parceljs.org/getting-started/migration/):

1. Upgraded Parcel and added the glob resolver plugin: `yarn add babel-plugin-transform-glob-import --dev`
2. Added `.parcel-cache` to my `.gitignore`
3. Changed `out-dir` to `dist-dir` in my command flags
4. Prepended `url:` to all my SVG imports (which don't use globs).

The glob imports we use are for .mp4 files. Our app's video imports look like this:
```jsx
import videos from '../../../../projects-data/**/*.mp4';
```

Prepending `url:` to this glob builds the app, but results in `videos` being an empty object. Omitting the prefix leaves Parcel 2 finding the files, but throwing a missing transformer error for mp4 files (as it should, since I think it's trying to build the videos into the bundle and that would be silly).

Judging from what little I know about Parcel 2, it seems like I should be using the `url:` prefix in my video glob import, but that the proposed plugin doesn't handle the prefix. So I don't think it handles my needs at this time.

issue_context.title: Add support for glob imports to Parcel 2
issue_context.body:
<!---
Thanks for filing an issue 😄 ! Before you submit, please read the following:

Search open/closed issues before submitting since someone might have asked the same thing before!
-->

# 🐛 bug report

<!--- Provide a general summary of the issue here -->
Parcel 2 does not return transformed URLs when importing raw files specified using a glob pattern from JavaScript with any of
```js
import asset from 'url:/assets/**/*';
import asset from 'url:/assets/*';
import asset from 'url:/assets/*.ext';
```

## 🎛 Configuration (.babelrc, package.json, cli command)

<!--- If describing a bug, tell us what your babel configuration looks like -->
**package.json**
```js
{
  "name": "test",
  "dependencies": {
    "parcel": "next"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@babel/core": "^7.0.0"
  }
}

```

## 🤔 Expected Behavior

<!--- Tell us what should happen -->
From what I understand from the old Parcel docs, an object containing a mapping of files to transformed URLs should be returned, such as the following:
```js
{
   'file-1': '/file-1.8e73c985.png',
   'file-2': '/file-1.8e73c985.png'
}
```

## 😯 Current Behavior

<!--- Tell us what happens instead of the expected behavior -->

<!--- If you are seeing an error, please include the full error message and stack trace -->
Parcel fails during bundling with the following error:
```
$ yarn parcel index.html
ℹ Server running at http://localhost:1234
Building index.html...
× Build failed.
@parcel/core: Failed to resolve 'url:/assets/*' from './index.html'
C:\Users\User\Workspace\test\index.html:1:20
> 1 | <html>
>   |       ^
  2 |   <head>
  3 |     <script>
@parcel/resolver-default: Cannot load file './assets/*' in './'.
Did you mean ./assets?
```

## 💁 Possible Solution

<!--- Not obligatory, but suggest a fix/reason for the bug -->
Related:
#4222
#4055

## 🔦 Context

<!--- How has this issue affected you? What are you trying to accomplish? -->

<!--- Providing context helps us come up with a solution that is most useful in the real world -->
I am writing a game using three.js and was trying to import my images so that I can load them as textures.

## 💻 Code Sample

<!-- Please provide a code repository, gist, code snippet or sample files to reproduce the issue -->
**Folder Structure**
```
/root
 |-- /assets
 |    |-- test.png
 |-- index.html
 |-- package.json
```
**index.html**
```html
<html>
	<head>
		<script>
			import assets from 'url:/assets/*';
			console.log(assets);
		</script>
	</head>
</body>
```

## 🌍 Your Environment

<!--- Include as many relevant details about the environment you experienced the bug in -->

| Software         | Version(s) |
| ---------------- | ---------- |
| Parcel           | 2.0.0-alpha.3.2 (also reproducible on 2.0.0-nightly.277+149c00b7) |
| Node             | v12.17.0 |
| npm/Yarn         | yarn 2.0.0-rc.33 |
| Operating System | Windows 10 1909 |

<!-- Love parcel? Please consider supporting our collective:
👉  https://opencollective.com/parcel/donate -->
comments:
> Parcel 2 doesn't support globs (yet).

Is there workaround to import multiple files for the time being? I need to access the generated file names dynamically. Is this also about the resolver, I mean can I simply add this functionality by creating my own resolver?

Something like https://www.npmjs.com/package/babel-plugin-transform-glob-import (the only downside: you need to manually clear the cache when changing one of the imported file)

>  Is this also about the resolver?

No, at the moment a resolver plugin can only return a single result, so this would need further further in core.

> No, at the moment a resolver plugin can only return a single result, so this would need further further in core.

Correction: the problem at the moment is that the resolver couldn't add the directory to the watcher.

Are there any plans to support this behaviour some time soon? This was one of the things I liked about parcel. I would keep using v1 since it's a lot easier, but it seems it's not very well supported (but neither is v2 it seems)

This would be a must too, especially for modular architecture in components, something like:

`import Modules from 'Modules/**/index.js'`
or
`import * as Modules from 'Modules/**/index.js'`

where **Modules** is an alias within package.json targeting **src/modules** directory.

This [https://github.com/devongovett/babel-plugin-transform-glob-import](https://github.com/devongovett/babel-plugin-transform-glob-import) seems to be the only one working with Parcel v2 but breaks the *import url:...* and also does not work with Parcel's aliases...

Another educated thumbs up for this feature, I was amazed when I first witnessed it working in parcel v1 and since then it became a staple in most of my javascript projects' architecture.

It's probably the only thing keeping me from moving to v2 😃

Parcel 2 is a big beast, and it's understandable that some features might not make it or may take some time to be migrated. Especially considering that Parcel is an open source project.

I think that instead of saying things like "we need this or I won't use parcel", it might be a good idea to say the reasons why it would be worth adding to Parcel 2.

A reason I personally see this as an interesting feature is when you are trying to include a wiki or blog post section in an application.

e.g.

```tsx
import wiki from "url:./docs/**/*.md"
console.debug("wiki", wiki)
```

In parcel v1, this (without the `url` flag) would output something like

```
{
  "introduction" : "markdown content", // file
  "getting-started": { // folder
    "step-1": "markdown-content", // file
    "step-2": "markdown-content", // file
    "step-2": "markdown-content", // file
  }
}
```

Perhaps in parcel 2, this could output a similar structure but with links to the bundled resources when used in conjunction with the `url` flag.

This should be addressed by #5933, which introduces a `@parcel/resolver-glob` plugin. It supports loading globs from within JS and CSS files. In JS, they can be synchronous or dynamic imports, and pipelines (e.g. `url:`) are supported. Because it's an actual Parcel plugin instead of a Babel plugin, the watcher and cache should invalidate automatically when a new file matching the glob is added. 😄
This is very cool and so nice to hear! 😄

To make use of this feature right away, set your parcel version to `nightly` (`next` is too old) and add this [`.parcelrc`](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/bdb43afa4aaab364f4018634bc8c0d6e7fc6c30c/packages/core/integration-tests/test/integration/glob-async/.parcelrc) to the root of your project.

Wanted to ask here rather than open a new issue as I've been following this thread and instructions here.

With `parcel` and `@parcel/resolver-glob` set to either `nightly` or `next`, async (e.g. `url:`) imports do not work.

So this works:
`import file from "foo/bar/*.ts"`

but this fails
`const files = import("foo/bar/*.ts")`

with the following error:
`ENOENT: no such file or directory, open 'D:\Projects\test\dist\\*.e674183c.js.1115428497'`

Is there anything to note about project setup  or parcel versions to get async dynamic imports to work?

Thanks!
@BarakChamo Can you open an new issue?
@mischnic I'm not sure what happened but the issue went away on `@nightly`, all good here 👍

review_comments:
I guess we should change the return type of `dependency.resolveFrom` to `FilePath`? It's always a string

https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/98c5902cefe1bba6c890da56f111e4b31b487c64/packages/core/core/src/public/Dependency.js#L111-L113
`dependency.loc` should be attached to the diagnostic

Not totally sure how I feel about mutating the dependency in the resolver, but we did it already for meta... Otherwise we'd need to move `isAsync` to the AssetGroup, but that's not available in the bundle graph. 😞
